title: Advanced Idioms
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Estos modismos avanzados te permiten entender las sutilezas y el lenguaje figurado de los negocios, dándote la verdadera fluidez de un nativo en entornos C-Level.

parts.visual:
Toma de Decisiones y Dificultades: 
- Bite the bullet (Tragar saliva / Afrontar una situación difícil e inevitable). 
Ej: We just have to bite the bullet and fire him. 
- Cut corners (Tomar atajos / Hacer las cosas mal o barato para ahorrar tiempo/dinero). 
Ej: They cut corners on safety, and now they are being sued. 
- In a nutshell (En pocas palabras / En resumen). 
Ej: In a nutshell, we are losing money.
parts.audio: Decision Making and Difficulties. 'Bite the bullet' means to face a difficult but unavoidable situation bravely. For example: We just have to bite the bullet and fire him. To 'Cut corners' means to do something poorly or cheaply to save time or money. For example: They cut corners on safety, and now they are being sued. 'In a nutshell' means in a few words or in summary. For example: In a nutshell, we are losing money.

parts.visual:
Progreso y Cambios: 
- Move the goalposts (Cambiar las reglas del juego cuando el proceso ya empezó, haciendo más difícil ganar). 
Ej: We almost finished the project, but the client moved the goalposts again. 
- Get off the ground (Despegar / Empezar a tener éxito). 
Ej: We need more funding to get this project off the ground. 
- Elephant in the room (El elefante en la habitación / Un problema enorme del que nadie quiere hablar). 
Ej: Let's address the elephant in the room: our CEO's resignation.
parts.audio: Progress and Changes. To 'Move the goalposts' means to unfairly change the rules or conditions of a process while it is happening. For example: We almost finished the project, but the client moved the goalposts again. 'Get off the ground' means to start being successful or to begin operating. For example: We need more funding to get this project off the ground. The 'Elephant in the room' is a huge, obvious problem that everyone is ignoring. For example: Let's address the elephant in the room: our CEO's resignation.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el modismo corporativo avanzado correcto.

questions.question: The meeting is going to be terrible, but we just have to bite the ____ and do it. (Afrontarlo valientemente).
questions.explanation: Bite the bullet = afrontar algo difícil e inevitable.

questions.question: If you ____ corners on quality, the customers will eventually notice. (Tomas atajos / Haces cosas mediocres para ahorrar).
questions.explanation: Cut corners = tomar atajos, sacrificar calidad por tiempo/dinero.

questions.question: To put it in a ____, the company is bankrupt. (En pocas palabras).
questions.explanation: In a nutshell = en resumen, en pocas palabras.

questions.question: It's impossible to please this client. Every time we finish, they ____ the goalposts. (Cambian las reglas del juego).
questions.explanation: Move the goalposts = cambiar las reglas injustamente.

questions.question: Before we talk about the new budget, let's address the ____ in the room: the massive debt. (El problema obvio que nadie menciona).
questions.explanation: Elephant in the room = el problema evidente pero ignorado.

questions.question: We have everything planned, but we need $50,000 to get the business off the ____. (Despegar / Empezar).
questions.explanation: Get off the ground = arrancar, despegar un proyecto o negocio.

questions.question: I don't know the exact number, but as a ____ of thumb, we spend 10% on marketing. (Regla general / Aproximación).
questions.explanation: Rule of thumb = regla general, estimación práctica.

questions.question: The negotiations went down to the ____. We signed the contract at 11:59 PM. (Hasta el último momento/Límite).
questions.explanation: Down to the wire = hasta el último minuto o límite de tiempo.

questions.question: I'm sorry, I can't talk right now. I'm completely ____ under with paperwork. (Inundado/Tapado de trabajo).
questions.explanation: Snowed under = saturado o enterrado bajo mucho trabajo.

questions.question: Our competitor is launching a new AI tool. We need to stay on our ____! (Estar alerta / Preparados).
questions.explanation: Stay on one's toes = mantenerse alerta y preparado.

questions.question: I am not going to sugarcoat it. The situation is bad. Let's call a spade a ____. (Llamar a las cosas por su nombre).
questions.explanation: Call a spade a spade = hablar claro, decir las cosas como son.

questions.question: He got the promotion because he always goes the extra ____ for his clients. (Da el esfuerzo extra).
questions.explanation: Go the extra mile = hacer un esfuerzo mayor al esperado.

questions.question: We are still in the ____ with this new technology. We don't know if it will work. (En la oscuridad / Ignorancia).
questions.explanation: Keep someone in the dark / Be in the dark = ignorar, no saber lo que pasa.

questions.question: This project is a bottomless ____. We keep putting money into it, but see no results. (Pozo sin fondo).
questions.explanation: Bottomless pit = pozo sin fondo (algo que consume recursos interminablemente).

questions.question: If we want to beat the competition, we need to think outside the ____. (Pensar de forma original/creativa).
questions.explanation: Think outside the box = pensar de forma innovadora o creativa.

questions.question: The new manager is a bit rough around the ____, but he knows what he's doing. (Tosco / Le falta pulirse).
questions.explanation: Rough around the edges = tosco, sin refinar, pero con potencial.

questions.question: By doing this, we can kill two birds with one ____. (Matar dos pájaros de un tiro).
questions.explanation: Kill two birds with one stone.

questions.question: I don't have the exact figures, but off the ____ of my head, I'd say $50,000. (De memoria / A simple vista).
questions.explanation: Off the top of my head = de memoria, sin comprobar los datos.

questions.question: We need to get all our ducks in a ____ before we sign the contract. (Organizar todo).
questions.explanation: Get one's ducks in a row = organizar todo, prepararse adecuadamente.

questions.question: I had a great presentation prepared, but the CEO stole my ____ by announcing the news first. (Me robó el protagonismo).
questions.explanation: Steal someone's thunder = robarle a alguien el momento de gloria, la atención o el protagonismo.
